title: "Just fill it in and I'll sign"
topic: Probity in training, research, audit and applications
stem:
You are an F2 doctor near the end of your placement. Your educational supervisor is very busy. She emails to say she hasn't had time to complete your end-of-placement report, and asks you to fill in her section yourself so she can "just sign it".

The report is used at your annual review.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Complete her section honestly, rating yourself fairly, as she asked.
options.brief: Honest ratings are still your judgement, not hers.
options.detailed: This is tempting because it's what she asked, and you might be fair. But it's still not her assessment, and signing it would misrepresent who made the judgement.

options.text: Offer to send her a summary of your achievements and evidence to help her write it.
options.brief: Saves her time without writing her assessment for her.
options.detailed: Many supervisors appreciate a summary of the evidence in your portfolio. This helps her without you writing her judgement. It ranks second because the first option keeps the assessment entirely hers.

options.text: Complete her section, rating yourself highly in every area.
options.detailed: This would misrepresent your performance in a report used to judge your progress. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Ask your foundation programme tutor for advice.
options.brief: Useful if she can't complete it, though less direct.
options.detailed: The tutor can advise on what's acceptable and help if she can't complete it in time. It ranks third because a direct, helpful reply may solve it.

options.text: Reply that you'd prefer her to complete it, and offer a short meeting.
options.brief: Respects her time while keeping the assessment hers.
options.detailed: Her report should reflect her judgement. Offering a short meeting, at a time that suits her, makes it easier for her to complete it properly.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you keep assessments honest when a busy supervisor suggests a shortcut.
explanation.keyDetails: The report should be her judgement. It is used at your annual review. She is busy, not dishonest.
explanation.reasoning: [E] keeps the assessment hers, [B] helps her without writing it, and [D] seeks advice. [A] writes her judgement for her, and [C] does so dishonestly.
explanation.competing: This is hard because [A] is honest in content. It ranks below the others because it still misrepresents who made the assessment.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, honesty in assessments and records of your training.
